column3: “The prince, prince he” is rendered “As for the prince, he … as prince.”
“To rebellion” is rendered “to the rebellious ones,” and “too much for you” as “Enough.”
“Sons of foreignness” is rendered “foreigners”; the Hebrew “they broke” is rendered as “you” in NASB.
“Lifted up my hand” is rendered “I have sworn.”
“Holy things of the holy things” is rendered “most holy.”
“The priests the Levites” is rendered “the Levitical priests.”
“Head-dresses” is rendered “turbans,” and “sweat” as “anything which makes them sweat.”
NASB repeats “into the outer court” as the Hebrew does; the LXX has it once.
“People will count” is rendered “seven days shall elapse.”
“It will become for them into an inheritance” is rendered “with regard to an inheritance for them.”
